plan.contextChunk: This figure is a heavily labeled diagram of a hyperbola opening left and right, centered at the origin of a coordinate system with arrowhead-tipped axes marked x at the right and y at the top. Two dark blue branches sweep away from the horizontal axis, one on each side. A pair of orange dashed lines cross at the center and run diagonally to the corners of the drawing, each tagged by a leader arrow reading "Asymptote" at the lower left and lower right. A teal dashed rectangle is centered on the origin, its vertical sides passing through the turning points of the two branches and its horizontal sides passing through two points on the vertical axis, with its corners sitting on the orange diagonals. A short red segment along the horizontal axis joins the two turning points and is labeled "Transverse axis" by an arrow pointing down onto it; a light blue segment along the vertical axis joins the top and bottom of the rectangle and is labeled "Conjugate axis." Dark blue dots at the ends of the red segment are each labeled "Vertex," light blue dots at the ends of the vertical segment are each labeled "Co-vertex," teal dots farther out along the horizontal axis are each labeled "Focus," and an orange marker at the crossing point is labeled "Center." Assembling every named element on one curve shows how the rectangle and its extended diagonals govern the directions the branches approach.

interactions.label: Transverse half-axis a
interactions.teaches: a sets where each branch turns: moving the vertices inward or outward shifts the red transverse axis and the closest approach of the branches, while the asymptote directions stay fixed if b is unchanged

interactions.label: Conjugate half-axis b
interactions.teaches: b controls the guide rectangle height and therefore the asymptote slopes ±b/a: increasing b opens the branches wider, decreasing b flattens them toward the x-axis, without moving the vertices

interactions.label: Construction guides
interactions.teaches: The dashed rectangle and asymptotes are construction scaffolding: hiding them leaves the same branches, revealing that the curve's wide-open shape is dictated by guides that are not part of the final graph

demo_steps.title: Meet the anatomy
demo_steps.narration: The hyperbola sits centered at the origin: vertices and foci on the x-axis, co-vertices on the y-axis, with the transverse (red) and conjugate (blue) axes meeting at the center. The dashed rectangle's corners lie exactly on the asymptotes.

demo_steps.title: Move the vertices with a
demo_steps.narration: Drag the transverse slider: the red axis stretches, the vertices slide along the x-axis, and both branches turn at new x-positions — while the rectangle height and asymptote slopes stay put. a alone decides where each branch bends.

demo_steps.title: Reshape the opening with b
demo_steps.narration: Now drag the conjugate slider: the rectangle grows taller, the asymptotes steepen, and the branches open wider — the vertices never move. b alone decides the direction each branch eventually travels.

demo_steps.title: Remove the scaffolding
demo_steps.narration: Switch to 'Curve only': the rectangle and asymptotes vanish but the branches are unchanged. The guides were never part of the hyperbola — they are the drafting tool that determines it.

Red transverse axis segment and light blue conjugate axis segment overlay the axes between their respective vertices. Color-code all markers to match their labels: dark blue vertices, light blue co-vertices, teal foci (positioned at ±c with c = √(a²+b²)), orange center. Keep every leader-arrow label from the original figure (Vertex, Co-vertex, Focus, Center, Transverse axis, Conjugate axis, Asymptote) but allow them to be toggleable or hover-clean if they crowd. In 'Curve only' mode, fade out rectangle, asymptotes, co-vertices, and their labels while keeping branches, vertices, foci, and axes.

authoredContext:
As with the ellipse, every hyperbola has two axes of symmetry. The transverse axis is a line segment that passes through the center of the hyperbola and has vertices as its endpoints. The foci lie on the line that contains the transverse axis. The conjugate axis is perpendicular to the transverse axis and has the co-vertices as its endpoints. The center of a hyperbola is the midpoint of both the transverse and conjugate axes, where they intersect. Every hyperbola also has two asymptotes that pass through its center. As a hyperbola recedes from the center, its branches approach these asymptotes. The central rectangle of the hyperbola is centered at the origin with sides that pass through each vertex and co-vertex; it is a useful tool for graphing the hyperbola and its asymptotes. To sketch the asymptotes of the hyperbola, simply sketch and extend the diagonals of the central rectangle. See the figure.

Key features of the hyperbola

This diagram illustrates the various components of a hyperbola centered at the origin, including the vertices, co-vertices, foci, transverse axis, conjugate axis, asymptotes, and the rectangular box used to construct the asymptotes.

In this section, we will limit our discussion to hyperbolas that are positioned vertically or horizontally in the coordinate plane; the axes will either lie on or be parallel to the x- and y-axes. We will consider two cases: those that are centered at the origin, and those that are centered at a point other than the origin.

discrepancies: labels are packed close to their features inside the plot instead of sitting in the open margins with the long, thin leader arrows that give the source its airy composition (e.g. 'Transverse axis' and 'Center' text sit right on top of the red segment area)
the source's leader arrows are thin black single strokes; the generated arrows are drawn with separate polygon arrowheads that render slightly chunky and gray (#555) rather than black
the added monospace equation readout box (x²/a² − y²/b² = 1, asymptote slopes) has no counterpart in the source, though it is pedagogically useful
evaluation.notes: Excellent recreation: every labeled part of the source (both vertices, both foci, both co-vertices, center, transverse/conjugate axes, rectangle, both asymptotes) is present with correct colors, correct geometry (rectangle corners lie exactly on the asymptotes), and rich pedagogical interactions (a/b sliders, guide toggle, step player); main weakness is the compressed label layout versus the source's spacious leader-line composition.
action_items: Push labels outward into the open margins with longer leader lines (as the source does) so text never crowds the curves, axis segments, or the rectangle interior.
Bump label font size from 12px to ~14px and use black leader lines to better match the source's legibility and stroke style.
Reposition the 'Transverse axis' label so its text and arrow do not overlap the right branch of the hyperbola.
